title: MM2H Silver Tier in 2026: What You Need and What It Really Costs
desc: The Silver tier is the entry point to Malaysia's federal MM2H programme. Here is what it asks for, what you actually pay, and the property side buyers often miss.
sections: Who the Silver tier is for

The Silver tier is the lowest of the three federal MM2H tiers. It suits retirees, remote earners with income from abroad, and families who want a long-stay base in Malaysia without committing the larger sums that Gold and Platinum need. It does not allow you to take a job in Malaysia, so it works best for people whose income comes from outside the country.

Since the programme was restructured in 2024, Silver applicants need a fixed deposit of USD 150,000 in a licensed Malaysian bank and a residential property purchase of at least RM600,000. The main applicant must be 25 or older. The pass runs for 5 years and can be renewed, and a spouse and children can usually be included under the same application. Applications go through a licensed MM2H agent approved by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC).
The costs on top of the deposit

The deposit is your own money and stays in your name, but it is not the only cost. Budget for the participation fee and visa fees for each family member, the agent's service fee, and the costs of buying a home: stamp duty, which is higher for foreign buyers, legal fees and loan costs if you borrow. Fee schedules have changed more than once, so ask your agent for the current list before you transfer anything.
The property side most people miss

RM600,000 is the MM2H minimum, but each state also sets its own minimum price for foreign buyers, and in many popular areas that limit is higher. Foreign purchases also need state consent, which adds time. The MM2H property is generally expected to be held for around 10 years, so pick a home you are happy to keep, or one that rents well while you are away.
take: For most of my clients the Silver tier is the sensible starting point: the deposit is manageable and RM600,000 to RM1 million buys a good condo in Kuala Lumpur, Penang or Johor Bahru. The mistake I see is choosing the home last. Check the foreign buyer limit for your area first, then shortlist homes that meet both limits and that you would happily hold for ten years.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ

title: MM2H vs Thailand Privilege Visa: What You Pay and What You Get Back
desc: Thailand's Privilege visa is a fee you spend; MM2H is mostly money you keep. A side-by-side look at the real cost of a long stay in each country.
sections: Thailand Privilege, formerly called Thailand Elite, is a membership. You pay a one-off fee and get a long-stay visa plus perks such as airport service. Malaysia's MM2H works the other way round: most of the money you put in is a fixed deposit and a property that you still own. That single difference changes how the two compare.

Thailand Privilege fees are paid once for the whole period. Reports in 2026 list Gold at THB 900,000 for 5 years, Platinum at THB 1.5 million for 10 years, Diamond at THB 2.5 million for 15 years, and the invitation-only Reserve at THB 5 million for 20 years. The cheaper Bronze tier closed to new applicants at the end of September 2026. Adding a family member costs extra on the higher tiers. The fee is not refunded when the membership ends.

MM2H's federal tiers ask for a fixed deposit of USD 150,000, USD 500,000 or USD 1 million, and a home of at least RM600,000, RM1 million or RM2 million, for a pass of 5, 15 or 20 years. The deposit stays in your name and earns interest, and the home is an asset you can live in, rent out and eventually sell. The true cost is the fees, the buying costs and what the money could have earned elsewhere.

If you only want a visa and plan to rent, Thailand's entry tier needs far less cash up front. If you want to own a home in the country anyway, MM2H can work out cheaper over time, because the money goes into a deposit and a property rather than a fee. Neither programme gives a path to citizenship, and work is only allowed on MM2H's Platinum tier.
take: Clients who compare the two often look only at the entry price. I ask them a different question: do you want to own a home here? If yes, MM2H turns most of your outlay into an asset, and Kuala Lumpur still offers more space per ringgit than Bangkok's prime areas. If you just want a few years of easy stays, Thailand's membership is simpler.
